suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-26 adds this relationship only as a bounded atopic-disease association. Atopic dermatitis, particularly persistent or severe phenotypes, is associated with increased risk of subsequent asthma in systematic-review evidence, but the association does not establish that every patient with atopic dermatitis develops asthma or that the skin disease caused an individual's asthma. Require documented atopic dermatitis phenotype, independently established asthma using appropriate pulmonary criteria, compatible chronology, and review of allergic rhinitis, family atopy, environmental exposure, smoking, occupational factors, infection, obesity, and other respiratory causes. Do not infer asthma from eczema, atopy, cough, or wheeze without objective evaluation.
evidenceGaps: Independent dermatologic documentation of atopic dermatitis and pulmonary documentation of asthma
Spirometry with bronchodilator testing or other appropriate objective asthma assessment
Atopic-dermatitis onset, persistence/severity, asthma onset, and longitudinal chronology
Assessment of allergic rhinitis, family atopy, environmental and occupational exposures, smoking, obesity, and other respiratory causes

Resolution of publication guard: Require documented atopic-dermatitis phenotype, objective asthma diagnosis, compatible chronology, and competing-cause review; do not infer asthma from eczema or atopy alone.

sourceReferences.citation: Li H, Dai T, Liu C, Liu Q, Tan C. Phenotypes of atopic dermatitis and the risk for subsequent asthma: A systematic review and meta-analysis. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2022;86(2):365-372. PMID 34384834. doi:10.1016/j.jaad.2021.07.064.
sourceReferences.note: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-26 systematic review/meta-analysis for the bounded atopic-dermatitis-eczema to asthma proposition. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source remains pending qualified-human review.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 34384834; systematic review/meta-analysis of atopic-dermatitis phenotypes and subsequent asthma risk; approved ME-26 guard requires independent asthma diagnosis, phenotype, chronology, and competing-cause review.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The cited meta-analysis supports a population-level association between selected atopic-dermatitis phenotypes and later asthma, without proving individual causation.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established; atopic phenotype, objective pulmonary findings, chronology, and alternative respiratory causes require individual review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Shared epithelial-barrier and type-2 inflammatory susceptibility may contribute to sequential atopic disease manifestations, but the individual relationship between dermatitis and asthma remains hypothesized rather than established.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The meta-analysis examines subsequent asthma risk across heterogeneous atopic-dermatitis phenotypes and does not prove that atopic dermatitis caused an individual's asthma.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent skin and asthma diagnoses; objective pulmonary testing; dermatitis phenotype and severity; chronology; allergic-rhinitis and family-atopy history; environmental/occupational exposure; smoking; obesity; and other respiratory causes.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: allergic rhinitis or other atopic disease
chronic infection or structural lung disease
vocal-cord dysfunction or other non-asthma wheeze

governanceNotes: SCOPE SPLIT DECISION 2026-09-28 - NOT CONSOLIDATED with the eczema identity, and the identity-duplication finding recorded in batches 80 and 82 is RETRACTED as erroneous at the evidence level. This identity is ATOPIC DERMATITIS specifically. Its registered route, atopic-dermatitis-eczema -> asthma at IMMUNE_MEDIATED, rests on the systematic review and meta-analysis 'Phenotypes of atopic dermatitis and the risk for subsequent asthma' (J Am Acad Dermatol. 2022;86(2):365-372, PMID 34384834, qualified-human verified 2026-09-02) and is scoped to ATOPIC DERMATITIS PHENOTYPES, so it may not be widened to eczema in general. The sibling identity eczema in skin.json owns the generic and iatrogenic eczematous eruptions and holds a separate qualified-human-verified route, psoriasis -> eczema, for PARADOXICAL ECZEMA INDUCED BY BIOLOGIC THERAPY for psoriasis (JAMA Dermatol. 2024;160(1):71-79, PMID 38055239), which is a drug-induced eczematous eruption and is not atopic dermatitis. Because the two identities carry two different verified disease routes, NO MERGE CAN PRESERVE BOTH MAPPINGS and the consolidation request was resolved as a scope split instead. SCOPE BOUNDARY RECORDED: no claim routed here may be widened to generic eczema, and no claim at the eczema identity may be extended to atopic dermatitis. The catalog alias 'atopic dermatitis' was added here and the sibling gained 'paradoxical eczema' and 'drug-induced eczema' so the two names resolve distinctly rather than to one another's scope.

The earlier batch-27 duplicate-scope rationale at the sibling identity, that authoring eczema to any of the dermatitis targets would create parallel pathways restating the same disease process under a synonym identity, is RETIRED as applied to these two identities: the two routes are not parallel restatements of one process. It may still apply to any proposed edge that would restate the dermatitis -> insomnia, cellulitis, impetigo or mood routes under this identity, and such an edge would still be refused as duplicate-scope.

Update 2026-09-28 (composite-scope adjudication of the sibling dermatitis identity, docs/modeling-debt-dispositions.md): THIS IDENTITY OWNS THE ATOPIC PSYCHIATRIC-MORBIDITY AND SLEEP WINDOW. The three dermatitis-side edges (dermatitis -> insomnia rank 1, -> depressive-disorder rank 4, -> anxiety-disorder rank 5) rest entirely on adult atopic-dermatitis anchors (Bawany 2021, Silverberg 2022, Fasseeh 2022, Mann 2020) and were superseded as claim windows under the composite dermatitis identity because that identity's claim contexts for atopic evidence are exhausted; the correctly-directed home for that evidence is here. The window may be authored HERE EXACTLY ONCE, after explicit adjudication of the preserved rel-dermatitis-to-insomnia, rel-dermatitis-to-depressive-disorder and rel-dermatitis-to-anxiety-disorder records and their registered PMIDs under the ME-29 reserved-evidence discipline, carrying the same guards the preserved records carry (cross-sectional anchors, documented itch-sleep and mood-itch bidirectionality, flare confounding, sedating-antihistamine medication confound, mediation-not-causation). The statement in the preceding note that an edge restating 'the dermatitis -> insomnia ... or mood routes' under this identity would be refused as duplicate-scope is SUPERSEDED AS TO THE INSOMNIA AND MOOD TARGETS ONLY, for exactly that one adjudicated authoring pass; the duplicate-scope refusal stands unchanged for the cellulitis and impetigo targets, which remain the dermatitis identity's generic windows.
